compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Bug `soppy-logophilic-husky` (3fa7-94ba-42aa-4623) showed CI can LOSE test results without
saying so. Two properties, both outliving that specific budget:

1. **Crashed workers silently drop tests.** Failing runs reported 16175 outcomes where the
   passing parent reported 16182; locally the gap was ~95 vs 183. The suite ran more tests
   than it reported, so a genuine failure inside a dropped test would have gone unseen.
2. **The event was misattributed.** A red build on `main` was investigated as a defect in the
   change under review (Gerrit 2098) because nothing named the real cause. `worker crashed` /
   `node down: Not properly terminated` is runner infrastructure failing, not a test verdict.

This is a known ecosystem edge, not a local quirk: `pytest-timeout#137` documents the
timeout-plus-xdist worker crash exactly; `pytest-xdist#466`/`#932` document lost coverage and
double-reported tests after a node dies.

**How mature OSS projects handle it.** LLVM `lit` makes "produced no result" a first-class
outcome — `UNRESOLVED`/`TIMEOUT` count as FAILURES, so the gap cannot exist. Jest fixed it in
the worker pool (`jest#13566`) after OOM-killed workers hung the run. For an OOM the framework
is already dead, so the signal is read from outside: exit 137 = SIGKILL, 139 = SIGSEGV. None of
these projects ask contributors to hand-maintain expected test counts.

## Scope boundary — CI matrix work is OWNED ELSEWHERE
A parallel session currently owns CI performance, the Python-version matrix and 3.14 adoption,
under an approved pattern (oldest/newest supported in the Gerrit Verified gate; intermediate
versions on the scheduled main sweep; macOS on the hot path but scoped to compatibility tests
while Ubuntu runs the full suite; Windows considered for the scheduled sweep). **This story
changes no matrix, no lane, and no runner count.** It is deliberately confined to detection
that is in-process and therefore free of CI latency. The wider OSS-alignment backlog — endpoint
Python versions, Windows, pre-merge CodeQL, widening Zizmor beyond `release.yml`, SHA-pinning
actions, `twine check` in the artifact probe, external link checking, dependency-bound sweeps,
diff coverage — is recorded separately for that owner and is OUT OF SCOPE here.

## Approach
Adopt the runner-level pattern; do not invent bespoke accounting.

**Rejected: reconciling outcome counts.** `pytest-xdist#932` shows crashed items are
rescheduled and can report twice, so the arithmetic can overcount as well as undercount, and
it would need hand-tuning for `-x`, `--maxfail` and `-k`/`-m` deselection. That is a
change-detector wearing an invariant's clothing.

**Primary — in-process, CI-agnostic, zero added latency.** A new plugin module implements
`pytest_testnodedown(node, error)` (xdist `newhooks.py:84`; xdist 3.8.0 is pinned here) and
records every abnormal exit — `error` is non-`None` when a node dies rather than finishing. At
`pytest_sessionfinish` it writes a red diagnostic naming the node id and the error, then
escalates `session.exitstatus` to `pytest.ExitCode.TESTS_FAILED`.

That escalation is an ESTABLISHED SEAM here, not a novelty: `tests/conftest.py:718-735` already
does exactly this for a leaked working tree, including the
`terminalreporter.write_line(..., red=True)` diagnostic and the `session.exitstatus`
assignment. This follows it. The plugin lives in its OWN module because `tests/conftest.py` is already a large shared test harness module (currently about 923 lines in the reviewed tree) and the new crash-detection logic needs to be isolated, unit-testable, and minimally wired; conftest only registers it. The repository module-size gate applies to `src/rebar/**/*.py`, not `tests/`, so no claim here depends on that gate enforcing a tests/conftest.py line ceiling.

**Secondary — the signal no in-process hook can see.** An OOM kill destroys the interpreter, so
`pytest` cannot report it. A small `scripts/` helper maps a process exit status to a named
cause (137 SIGKILL/likely-OOM, 139 SIGSEGV, 124 timeout) and prints a human-readable line. The
LOGIC lives in `scripts/` where it is unit-testable and runnable by hand; the workflow touch is
a single call, keeping the collision surface with the CI owner to one line.

**Portability.** Detection is in-process: it fires under `make test` on a laptop, under any CI
provider, and with no CI at all. The exit-status helper is a plain script, not a
GitHub-Actions-only capability. Nothing here is triggered solely by one CI system.

## Testing
Drive a REAL crash, not a mock: a generated test calling `os._exit(1)` mid-run, in a child
pytest launched through `tests/_nested_pytest.py::run_nested_pytest` — the single sanctioned
nested-launch site (story `phantasmal-enhanced-barnowl`) — under `-n 2`. Assert on the child's
returncode and output so the oracle exercises the real hook rather than a stub.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A crashed worker fails the run and names itself: a nested run whose test calls
      `os._exit(1)` under `-n 2` exits non-zero and its output carries the worker id and the
      node error; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_crash_guard.py -k names_the_dead_worker`.
- [ ] A crash cannot be masked by green tests — the same nested run with every OTHER test
      passing still exits non-zero; checked by `-k not_masked_by_passing_tests`. This is the
      property that failed in the incident: 16175 green outcomes beside 7 vanished ones.
- [ ] The verdict comes from the HOOK, not from scraping output:
      `grep -c "node down\|worker crashed" tests/_crash_guard.py` returns 0, and the module
      references `pytest_testnodedown`; checked by that grep plus the guard test.
- [ ] Single-process runs are untouched: a nested run WITHOUT `-n` over a passing test exits 0
      and prints no crash diagnostic; checked by `-k single_process_is_untouched`.
- [ ] The exit-status helper names 137, 139 and 124 with distinct human-readable causes and
      exits 0 for status 0; checked by `pytest tests/scripts/test_classify_runner_exit.py -q`,
      which invokes it directly with no CI involved.
- [ ] `tests/conftest.py` receives only the minimal plugin registration/import needed for the crash guard; the substantive logic stays in `tests/_crash_guard.py`. This is checked by reading `git diff -- tests/conftest.py` in-session. The `src/rebar` module-size CI gate is unchanged and is not claimed to verify tests/conftest.py.
- [ ] No matrix, lane or runner-count change: `git diff origin/main -- .github/workflows/` adds
      at most one invocation line plus comments, and changes no `python-version`, `os:` or
      `matrix:` key; checked by reading that diff.
- [ ] No regression: `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, and
      `pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py -q`
      passes unedited.

## Plan-review clarification (2026-09-07)

The earlier conftest size wording was wrong: `tests/conftest.py` is already roughly 923 lines in the reviewed tree, and the module-size gate reads `.github/module-size-limit.txt` only for `src/rebar/**/*.py`, not for tests/. The observable proxy is therefore not a false under-cap claim; it is that this story adds only the minimal conftest registration/import while all crash-guard behavior lives in `tests/_crash_guard.py` and is covered by its own tests. The worked example is: inspect `git diff -- tests/conftest.py` and confirm it is registration-only, then rely on `make verify` for the unchanged `src/rebar` module-size gate and the new targeted tests for behavior.

The exit-status helper's canonical-path evidence will be recorded from the Gerrit change that
lands this story: change number, `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and submit timestamp. The
helper also has direct in-session evidence from `pytest tests/scripts/test_classify_runner_exit.py -q`,
which invokes `scripts/classify_runner_exit.py` without CI.
